title: ElasticMM: Efficient Multimodal LLMs Serving with Elastic Multimodal Paral

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Abstract claims 'reducing TTFT by up to 6.8× and achieving 5.1–7.2× higher throughput', but the Introduction (line near contributions) says 'reduces TTFT by up to 4.2× and achieves a 3.2×–4.5× throughput improvement', and the experimental section (Section 4.2) reports maximum improvements of 4.5× throughput and 4.2× TTFT reduction. The abstract numbers are inconsistent with the body of the paper and appear fabricated or exaggerated.

The paper uses LLaMA3.2-Vision-11B and cites [21], which is 'Llama Guard 3 Vision: Safeguarding human-AI image understanding conversations' (Chi et al., arXiv:2411.10414). That is a safety classifier, not the base LLaMA 3.2 Vision model. The correct reference for the vision-language model is missing or misattributed.

The text states 'Zhang et al. [61] proposed a similar two-tier separation in 2024 but lacked elastic scheduling.' The reference list ends at [60], so [61] does not exist. This is either a missing reference or a fabricated citation.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 3.1, burst tolerance definition and Equation (1)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text defines burst tolerance as 'the difference between peak load and idle capacity normalized by total instances', but Equation (1) defines bt(i) = N_i^{peak} / N_i^{avg}, a ratio of peak to average instances. The textual definition does not match the equation, and the concept of idle capacity is not used. This is an internal logical inconsistency.

predicted_errors.error_location: Appendix B.9, Empirical Validation table and accompanying text
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The appendix reports 100% identical outputs (bit-identical) and average token probability differences < 1e-8. Earlier in Proposition 1, the theoretical bound is ε_max ≈ 1e-7 for fp16. Achieving diffs an order of magnitude smaller than the theoretical bound and perfect bit-identity across different parallelism configurations is highly implausible and likely fabricated. The claimed 100% bit-identity is also unrealistic for non-trivial model parallelism.
